name: Never Mind the Bollocks Here’s the Sex Pistols

info.desc: Never Mind the Bollocks, Here's the Sex Pistols (often shortened to Never Mind the Bollocks) is the only studio album by the English punk rock band the Sex Pistols. It was released on October 28, 1977 through Virgin Records. As a result of the Sex Pistols' volatile internal relationships, the band's lineup saw changes during the recording of the album. Original bass guitarist Glen Matlock left the band early in the recording process, and while he is credited as a co-writer on all but two of the tracks, he only played bass and sang backing vocals on one track, "Anarchy .

podcast.body: Another reissue of this album is being released to coincide with its 40th anniversary. The album has been reissued numerous times, each time at an increased price. "otra redición de nevermind de volos de los sextpistols coinciendo de 40 aniversarios o sea yo ya no sé cuántas veces han reditado este disco cada vez a más precio volvemos a tener otra redición de nevermind de volos."

Glenn Matlock, a founding member, co-wrote no fewer than 10 of the 12 songs on the band's sole album. He was considered a major creative force, capable of shaping melody out of the band's raw anger. "He co-wrote no fewer than 10 of the 12 songs in the Sex Pistols one in only album, Never Mind the Ballocks."

podcast.body: Released on November 28, 1977. A radio commercial for the album was produced, with the word "bollocks" edited out to avoid offending listeners. This record would go on to define the original British punk rock era and is credited with launching a billion bands worldwide, despite being the band's only album. "It would be the record that defined the original British punk rock era and an album that launched a billion bands around the world."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.body: Released on October 28, 1977, this album's cover features a solid day-glow background, with the full title "Never Mind the Bollocks Here's the Sex Pistols" spelled out in a mix of different fonts and upper/lower case letters, resembling a ransom note. Two versions exist: one with a pink background and another with yellow. The artist, Jamie Reid, developed this ransom note style while working for *Suburban Press*. The title was changed in mid-1977 from an initial concept of "God Save the Sex Pistols" after guitarist Steve Jones heard fans using the phrase "Never Mind the Bollocks," meaning "Stop Talking Rubbish." "The first three lines are different fonts, while the band's name is styled in a mix of upper and lower case letters, reminiscent of a ransom note made out of cut up letters from a newspaper."

podcast.body: This album was recorded while Glenn Matlock was still a member of the band. Sid Vicious, who replaced Matlock in February 1977, was not featured on the recording. "He wasn't on the Nevermind the Bollocks album. Glenn Matlock was still a member when that was recorded."

podcast.body: This album was used by Zack de la Rocha to teach Tim Commerford how to play bass in grade seven, initiating Commerford's musical journey. "Zach taught Tim how to play bass along with the six pistols never mind the ballaks album."
